papers.zh: 非物质文化遗产保护中体现的虚拟现实人种学：羌年社区共创及其对文化知识和态度的影响
papers.en: Embodied virtual reality ethnography in intangible cultural heritage preservation: community co-creation of the Qiang New Year festival and its impact on cultural knowledge and attitudes
papers.absEn: The Qiang New Year festival, a core intangible cultural heritage (ICH) of China’s Qiang ethnic group, faces an existential crisis due to accelerated modernization and intergenerational discontinuity. This study explores a preservation pathway integrating embodied virtual reality (VR) ethnography with community-based co-design. Over 8 months of fieldwork, we developed a high-fidelity immersive VR experience rendering the ritual structure and narrative texture of the festival in a multisensory manner, enabling embodied participation through experiential learning. A quasi-experimental design (N = 200) employed a content-equivalent control: participants were randomly assigned to either a VR condition or a slideshow control, with both exposed to identical cultural content (ritual knowledge, symbolic systems, and contextual background), thereby isolating the medium’s immersion effect from content exposure. Results demonstrated significant advantages for the VR group in cultural knowledge acquisition (15-item test: VR post-test M = 12.9 vs. Control M = 9.8; p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 1.3) and heritage attitude (5-point scale difference ≈0.7; p < 0.001, η 2 = 0.19). VR participants also reported significantly higher immersive presence and emotional engagement. Post-experiment technology acceptance model (TAM) surveys and follow-up interviews (n = 40, κ = 0.83) indicated high perceived ease of use and enjoyment even among initially skeptical participants. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) analysis (SRMR = 0.063, CR > 0.80, AVE >0.50) validated the extended TAM structure and revealed a significant indirect effect of cultural immersion on heritage support intentions via cultural identification (β = 0.24, 95% CI [0.14, 0.35]). These findings offer a testable framework for integrating embodied VR and community co-design into ICH education, highlighting the distinct roles of knowledge transmission and affective identification in fostering preservation intentions.
papers.abstract: 羌年是中国羌族的核心非物质文化遗产（ ICH ） ，由于加速现代化和代际间断，面临着生存危机。本研究探索了一种将嵌入式虚拟现实（ VR ）民族志与基于社区的共同设计相结合的保存途径。 经过8个月的实地考察，我们开发了高保真沉浸式VR体验，以多感官的方式呈现节日的仪式结构和叙事纹理，通过体验式学习实现具体参与。 准实验设计（ N = 200 ）采用了内容等效对照：参与者被随机分配到VR条件或幻灯片对照，两者都暴露于相同的文化内容（仪式知识、符号系统和语境背景） ，从而将媒体的沉浸效应与内容暴露隔离开来。 结果表明， VR组在文化知识获取（ 15项测试： VR测试后M = 12.9 vs.对照M = 9.8 ； p < 0.001 ， Cohen's d = 1.3 ）和遗传态度（ 5分制差异≈ 0.7 ； p < 0.001 ， η 2 = 0.19 ）方面具有显著优势。VR参与者还报告了更高的沉浸感和情感参与度。 实验后技术接受模型（ TAM ）调查和随访访谈（ n = 40 ， κ = 0.83 ）表明，即使在最初持怀疑态度的参与者中，也具有很高的易用性和享受感。 偏最小二乘结构方程建模（ PLS-SEM ）分析（ SRMR = 0.063 ， CR > 0.80 ， AVE > 0.50 ）验证了扩展的TAM结构，并通过文化鉴定揭示了文化沉浸对遗产支持意图的显著间接影响（ β = 0.24 ， 95 ％ CI [0.14 ， 0.35] ）。 这些发现为将具体的VR和社区共同设计整合到ICH教育中提供了一个可测试的框架，突出了知识传播和情感识别在培养保护意图方面的不同作用。

papers.zh: 仪器的开发和试点验证测量Z世代对节日活动的行为意图
papers.en: Development and Pilot Validation of an Instrument Measuring Generation Z's Behavioral Intention Towards Festival Events
papers.authors: Ayu Rohaidah Ghazali, Wan Soraya Wan Abdul Ghani, Nurakmal Ramli et al.
papers.absEn: Generation Z has become an important consumer segment in the festival industry; therefore, there is a need to develop a reliable instrument to measure the factors influencing their behavioral intention towards festival events. The study aimed to design and conduct a preliminary validation of a measurement instrument comprising four constructs: media influence, social interaction, festival image, and behavioral intention. A quantitative pilot study was conducted with 36 Generation Z respondents, and the data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Cronbach’s Alpha. The results revealed satisfactory internal consistency for all constructs (? = 0.864-0.933), indicating that the proposed instrument is reliable and suitable for future large-scale empirical investigations. The validated instrument provides a methodological base for future research on Generation Z festival behavior.
papers.abstract: Z世代已成为节日行业的重要消费群体，因此需要开发一种可靠的工具来衡量影响他们对节日活动的行为意图的因素。该研究旨在设计和进行测量仪器的初步验证，该仪器包括四个结构：媒体影响、社交互动、节日形象和行为意图。 对36名Z世代受访者进行了定量试点研究，并使用描述性统计数据和Cronbach's Alpha对数据进行分析。结果显示所有构建体的内部一致性令人满意（ ？ = 0.864-0.933 ） ，表明所提出的仪器是可靠的，适用于未来的大规模实证研究。经过验证的仪器为未来Z世代节日行为的研究提供了方法论基础。
